{# Social and search metadata. LinkedIn's post inspector, Slack, X and Google all want the same things: an absolute og:image at least 1200x627, an absolute og:url, and a title and description that say what the page is. Everything below is derived from the page and mkdocs.yml, so a page only needs to override `description` (and, rarely, `og_image`) in its front matter. The card is 2400x1260 - twice the 1200x630 that LinkedIn, Slack and X crop to - and is rendered from docs/img/og-card.svg. The file name carries the size so that a change to the artwork is a new URL, which is what makes the crawlers refetch instead of serving their cached copy. #} {% extends "base.html" %} {% block extrahead %} {% set meta = page.meta if page and page.meta else {} %} {% set site = config.site_name %} {% set page_title = page.title if page and page.title else site %} {% set og_title = meta.og_title if meta.og_title else (site if page_title == site else page_title ~ " - " ~ site) %} {% set og_desc = meta.description if meta.description else config.site_description %} {% set og_image = meta.og_image if meta.og_image else 'img/og-card-2400.png' %} {% if not og_image.startswith('http') %} {% set og_image = config.site_url ~ og_image.lstrip('/') %} {% endif %} {% set canonical = page.canonical_url if page and page.canonical_url else config.site_url %} {% if not meta.og_image %} {% endif %} {% endblock %}
